title: Zero-section Tate comparison and affine-refinement compatibility
statement:
Work in the finite coefficient setting of [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $A=\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, and let $f:X\to Y$ be separated, of finite type and smooth of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use $\omega_h=Rh^!A$ and the exceptional inverse image and derived pullback of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], with the finite Tate sheaves $A_T(d)$ of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

For each finite-type affine open $V\subseteq Y$, set $X_V=X\times_YV$, $j_V:X_V\hookrightarrow X$, $W_V=X_V\times_VX_V$, with first projection $p_{1,V}$, diagonal $\Delta_V$, normal bundle $\pi_V:N_V\to X_V$ and zero section $z_V$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-open-immersion, def-pur-normal-bundle]. Let $\rho_V,\alpha_V,\delta_V$ be the canonical restriction, diagonal base-change and normalized DNC maps specified in [lem-pur-affine-target-diagonal-dnc]; $C(g,s)=Ls^*\omega_g$ is [def-pur-section-invariant]. Restriction of the canonical vector-bundle purity comparison [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] to $z_V$, followed by the finite-coefficient Tate pullback comparison $Lz_V^*A_{N_V}(d)\cong A_{X_V}(d)$ of [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists], is a canonical isomorphism
$$\beta_V:C(\pi_V,z_V)=Lz_V^*\omega_{\pi_V}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{X_V}(d)[2d].$$
Together with the canonical identification $Lj_V^*A_X(d)\cong A_{X_V}(d)$ of the same [det-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients-twists], it defines the specified local isomorphism
$$\theta_V=\beta_V\delta_V\alpha_V^{-1}\rho_V:
Lj_V^*\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{X_V}(d)[2d].$$
For every inclusion of finite-type affine target opens $V'\subseteq V$, put $a:X_{V'}\hookrightarrow X_V$. There is the canonical identification of section pairs
$$(W_V\times_{X_V,p_{1,V}}X_{V'}\to X_{V'},\Delta_V\times_{X_V}X_{V'})\cong(W_{V'}\to X_{V'},\Delta_{V'}),$$
and $N_{V'}\cong N_V\times_{X_V}X_{V'}$ with its zero section. Under these identifications and the canonical source and Tate restriction maps, $\rho_V,\alpha_V,\delta_V,\beta_V$ restrict to the respective maps for $V'$. In particular $\theta_V|_{X_{V'}}=\theta_{V'}$, compatibly with further affine restriction.
For any two finite-type affine opens $V_1,V_2\subseteq Y$, their intersection has a cover by finite-type affine opens $V'$, and on every such $V'$ the restrictions of $\theta_{V_1}$ and $\theta_{V_2}$ both equal $\theta_{V'}$. No affineness of $V_1\cap V_2$, and no absolute separatedness of $X,Y$, is assumed.

proof.text: Construct a normalized chart for every finite-type affine target open using the integration-normalized chart existence theorem.
For nested affine opens use all four factor equations from chart compatibility. Cancel adjacent source, section and normal comparisons in the four-factor composite to prove Agrees.
Cancel the source comparison in Agrees to identify every restricted orientation with the smaller chart orientation. Applying this identification twice proves successive restriction.

Use the Mathlib affine-open basis on the intersection. Local finite type of aY makes each affine open satisfy the required appTop finite-type condition. The two restrictions both equal its chart orientation.
